title: Security response headers and cookie hardening are incomplete

original_titles.title: CSP, HSTS and Permissions-Policy are not deployed anywhere
No CSP, HSTS or Permissions-Policy headers
HSTS missing; no __Secure- cookie prefix; Secure flag tied only to environment=='production'
No CSP defined (inline-script ban, worker-src) anywhere

problem: main.py adds nosniff and Referrer-Policy but does not set CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors or Permissions-Policy. CORS allow_credentials is enabled at application scope, and secure cookie behavior depends on environment configuration without a deployment assertion.
impact: XSS in challenge fixtures or another future rendering defect has a larger impact without CSP; clickjacking and transport downgrade protections are not explicitly enforced.

evidence_paths: frontend build: inline scripts and asset policy
verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Define a production CSP with nonce/hash strategy; start with default-src self, object-src none, base-uri self, frame-ancestors none, form-action self and narrowly scoped connect-src/style-src/font-src.
Set HSTS on HTTPS production responses with a tested max-age; use frame-ancestors in CSP and X-Frame-Options as a legacy fallback; add Permissions-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options.
Split public CORS routes from authenticated routes where possible. Keep exact allowed origins and avoid credentials for public read-only routes.
Use __Host-/__Secure- cookie prefixes where deployment permits; enforce Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite and host-only scope at production startup.
Add header tests for success/error/redirect/static responses and a production staging scan.

acceptance_criteria: Security headers are present on all production responses.
Refresh cookie attributes match production HTTPS requirements.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
